subject: zoology_2
question_text: Distinguish between the blind spot and the yellow spot.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Blind spot
steps.why: Where the optic nerve leaves there is no room for receptor cells, so that patch of retina cannot see.
common_mistakes: Writing that the blind spot has few receptors. It has none.
Placing it at the centre of the retina.
steps.memory_tip: Where the nerve leaves, nothing is seen.
steps.margin_note: Write the two spots as two rows.
lines: The blind spot is the site of the retina
where the optic nerve exits the eyeball.
It has no photoreceptor cells, so no image

steps.label: Yellow spot
steps.why: Cones packed close together at one point give the sharpest and most detailed vision.
common_mistakes: Giving the yellow spot rods. It contains only cones.
Leaving out that it gives sharp vision.
steps.memory_tip: Yellow spot has only cones, so it sees sharpest.
steps.margin_note: Mirror the structure of the first row.
lines: The yellow spot is the posterior portion

lines.text: Only cones, so it gives sharp central vision

insider_note: One spot has no photoreceptors and one has only cones. Say which cells each has — that is the difference being marked.
